description:
## Why

The workspace ships executable validators and linters for X.509 certs alongside policy-selection machinery. Where each rule lives — fast Rust code vs OSCAL JSON — has been decided case-by-case across `pkix-path`, `pkix-revocation`, `pkix-profiles`, `pkix-lint`. Codifying the split prevents future drift.

## The rule

**Standards-body technical specifications → fast Rust validator/lint code.**
**Policy choices → OSCAL Profiles (JSON or Rust constants producing the same shape).**

### What's a standards-body technical spec

- IETF RFCs (5280, 6125, 6960, 8551, 4518, 5755, 6962, 9162, ...)
- ITU-T X.509 (upstream of RFC 5280)
- ISO standards where they govern cert structure

### What's a policy choice

- Which standards-body specs to enforce in a given deployment
- Combinations / bundles (CA/B Forum TLS BR, S/MIME BR, Code Signing BR; Mozilla CA Policy; Apple/Microsoft/Chrome Root Program; DoD PKI)
- Deprecations of RFC-permitted things by industry consensus (no SHA-1, no MD5, no 1024-bit RSA, no CN-only identity, no certain extensions)
- Overrides and parameter values (validity-cap dates, allowed-algorithm tables, key-size floors, identity-tier required-field tables)

## What this means per crate

| Crate | Standards-body content | Policy content |
|---|---|---|
| `pkix-path` | RFC 5280 §6, RFC 6125 | (none — gates only) |
| `pkix-revocation` | RFC 5280 §5/§6.3, RFC 6960 | (none — checks only) |
| `pkix-revocation-http` | (transport mechanics) | (none) |
| `pkix-profiles` | `BasicTlsProfile` (RFC 5280 + 6125 + serverAuth EKU), `BasicSmimeProfile` (RFC 8551 §3) | (none after PKIX-amgn.4 lands the strip) |
| `pkix-lint` | RFC-conformance Lint Catalog (Rust `Lint` impls) | (none — emits findings) |
| `pkix-ct` | RFC 6962 / RFC 9162 | (none) |
| `pkix-ac` | RFC 5755 | (none) |
| `pkix-profiles-cabf` | (none) | CA/B Forum TLS BR, S/MIME BR, CS BR Profile types |
| `pkix-lint-cabf` | (none) | `cabf.br.tls` / `cabf.br.smime` Lint bundles (OSCAL Profiles, possibly with Rust constants producing the same shape) |

## Edge cases (already settled by this rule)

1. **Industry deprecations of RFC-permitted things.** RFC 5280 permits SHA-1 signatures; consensus rejects them. The "no SHA-1" rule is a policy choice → OSCAL Profile (e.g., `cabf.br.tls` excludes SHA-1 from the allowed-algorithms parameter). `pkix-path` executes whatever `ValidationPolicy` bits get set; the Profile decides which bits to set.

2. **Optional RFC bits that some Profiles require.** RFC 5280 §6.1 makes `cRLSign` on intermediates optional; PKITS-conformant profiles want it. `ValidationPolicy` gains a flag (`require_crl_sign_on_cas`, per PKIX-0x9z). The fast Rust path enforces what the flag asks; whether the flag is on is a Profile decision.

3. **Non-IETF standards that are de facto RFC-like.** CA/B Forum BRs are not IETF RFCs but are technical specifications for public-CA TLS at standards-document level of rigor. Under this rule they are classified as POLICY because they are authored by an industry forum, not a standards body. They live in `-cabf` reference crates marked not-authoritative.

## Out of scope

- IETF drafts (pre-RFC) — treated as policy until they reach RFC status.
- Vendor-specific protocols built on X.509 (e.g., 802.1AR DevID) — case-by-case; default to policy.
- Pure encoding crates (`x509-cert`, `der`, etc.) — those handle RFC structural encoding which is upstream of this question.

## Relationship to other stances

- **Extends `PKIX-amgn` (framework-not-policy):** RFC-baseline content stays in main crates; CA/B Forum / vendor policy goes to `-cabf` reference crates. This stance adds the "what counts as RFC-baseline" definition.
- **Extends `PKIX-ztmr` (OSCAL as source of truth):** OSCAL is the canonical authoring format for *policy choices*; not for *rule definitions*. Rule definitions are Rust.
- **Confirms AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6.** This stance is the per-rule operational form of the framework/policy split.

## Filed by

Maintainer (Mark) 2026-05-11 in conversation establishing the rule.
title: Stance: standards-body specs in fast Rust validators, policy choices in OSCAL Profiles
